title: Totality, finiteness, and complete index sets

based_on.title: Computability theory
based_on.pages: Version 2024-02-25; §17.2, printed/PDF p.72, Propositions17.4–17.5; positive-case sign in Proposition17.5 corrected; infinitude by complementation

summary: Classify totality and infinite domains as complete universal second-level problems, and finite domains as a complete existential second-level problem.
abstract: A program may halt on every input, on infinitely many inputs, or on only finitely many. All three questions are undecidable, but the arithmetical hierarchy distinguishes their exact difficulty. Totality and infinitude are complete for the second universal level, while finiteness is complete for the second existential level. The proofs turn an arbitrary definition at one of these levels into a program index by a terminating translation. For totality, the program searches separately for each requested witness. For finiteness, it halts on an input only after every candidate through that input has been refuted. A permanent candidate then bounds the domain, while the absence of one makes the domain infinite. These constructions prove both directions of each reduction and show why a displayed quantifier pattern or Rice’s theorem alone does not establish an exact classification.
